title: Uganda Climate Intelligence Framework (UCIF)
description:
Uganda Climate Intelligence Framework (UCIF)

This repository contains the complete, reproducible pipeline and analysis code behind the study "A National Climate Anomaly Intelligence System for Uganda: Ground-Truth Validation, Risk Nowcasting, and Long-Term Climate Change Assessment."

Core Methodology

The framework establishes a ground-truth-honest benchmark of unsupervised anomaly detection algorithms validated against a curated national disaster register. It extends the historical record with century-scale in-situ climate trends and addresses the 1990–2007 observing collapse through an independent NASA POWER gap-fill, ensuring continuity in the climate record.

Analytical Components

The system derives multiple layers of climate intelligence:

  • Drought indices: Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI)
  • Impact linkage: Statistical relationships between climate anomalies and cereal-yield variability
  • Severity assessment: The UCASI (Uganda Climate Anomaly Severity Index) for risk quantification
  • Explainability: SHAP-based interpretation of model outputs

Version 1.1: Forward-Looking Operational Layers

This release adds four operational components for proactive climate risk management:

  1. Drought Early Warning: SPI-6 trajectory analysis with decline-run detection rules
  2. Yield Impact Forecast: Growing-season SPI-3 regression model for agricultural planning
  3. Seasonal Climate Outlook: SEAS5 ensemble forecasts downscaled via Open-Meteo API
  4. Automated Climate Risk Bulletin: Narrative synthesis of all layers for decision support

Reproducibility

Every numerical result reported in the study is computed by the pipeline and cross-checked against persisted artifacts. The manuscript and code form an integrated, auditable system where all claims are traceable to their computational sources.
